text:
Zach Hyman is back. Oilersnation (Daily Faceoff Edmonton) reported that he returns to the lineup tonight against Vancouver after an injury absence that headlines framed as a test of Edmonton's forward depth. He has played only six games this season, with one goal, so his numbers say almost nothing yet. What matters is who he was: a 31-goal scorer in 58 games last season, the forward who lives at the net front next to McDavid.

The small sample still has a hint. His own chances in those six games, a bit over a goal of expected value per 60 minutes, are lower than last season's elite rate but still those of a scorer, and Evolving-Hockey had him among the best play drivers in the league in 2025-26 (98th percentile among forwards), with the caveat that he plays with the best teammates there are. He is not a speed or shot-power player; his game is getting to the crease and staying there. Our projection, assuming he plays every remaining game, is about 25 goals. The thing to watch is whether he steps straight back beside McDavid or eases in lower in the lineup.
headline: Zach Hyman returns to the net front
